clue.text: A blow to the Conservatives ?

parts.note: a 'blow' is a gust of air, and something that brings reform is a setback for those who resist it; the phrase also recalls a Conservative prime minister's 1960 speech

explanation.surface: A setback dealt to the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'blow' looks like a defeat for the party, but it is a gust: the phrase is from Harold Macmillan's 1960 speech in Cape Town, and Macmillan was himself a Conservative prime minister. Reform is by nature unwelcome to conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind is a blow of air, and the phrase means a tide of reform, the kind of shift any conservative resists.

clue.text: Carry on about a way of losing useful material

indicators.note: the words for carrying on go around the next pieces, as 'about' means surrounding here

parts.note: to carry on a war is to wage it
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone continuing a method that throws away good material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on' reads as 'continue', but it is WAGE, as in waging a campaign; 'about' puts A and ST inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastage is the loss of material through waste, leakage or wear.

clue.text: Club.(not the PEN one)

parts.note: PEN is a famous writers' association, a club for those who use pens; the club meant here is one swung on a golf course

explanation.surface: A club, specifically not the literary society of writers.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN is the international association of writers. The golfing club wanted is an old lofted iron, roughly today's nine-iron, and its name happens to start with NIB, the point of a pen, which adds to the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old Scottish name for a golf iron with a steeply angled face, used for lofted shots.

clue.text: In a' kind' of survey I give the direction

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the survey word, since 'In' tells us one piece sits within another

parts.note: the Ordnance Survey is Britain's national mapping agency

explanation.surface: A surveyor working on a map who also points the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is the British government's map-making body, so ORDNANCE is the 'kind of survey'; 'In' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative order or decree, a direction issued by those in power.

clue.text: All the best" from the Dairy Show

definitions.meaning: the pick of anything, the choicest part
a dairy product, the rich part of milk that rises to the top

explanation.surface: Best wishes sent from an agricultural exhibition of milk and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dairy Show was a London exhibition of dairy farming; 'All the best' looks like a sign-off but is the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the crème de la crème' gives the sense of the choicest few, and the fatty top layer of milk is the dairy sense.

clue.text: Hugs in a way to cause terrible pain

indicators.note: 'in a way' suggests the letters of the preceding words are rearranged in some other manner

explanation.surface: Being hugged in a certain manner hurts badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' signals the anagram of HUGS IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering.

clue.text: Nearly all the fascination comes from the love of France

definitions.text: Nearly all the fascination comes from the love of France

parts.words: Nearly all the fascination comes from the love of France
parts.note: the French for 'the love' makes up every letter but the first of a word for fascination or allure

explanation.surface: Most of the allure of the place derives from French romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The French L'AMOUR, 'the love' in France, is all of the answer except its first letter G, so 'nearly all' of the fascination word does literally come from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring charm or fascination.

clue.text: Wood can be so perverse!

definitions.meaning: timber whose fibres run across rather than along it
contrary, cantankerous, awkward to deal with

explanation.surface: An exasperated woodworker complaining that timber is contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber with an irregular fibre is hard to work, and figuratively a stubborn, contrary person is called the same.

clue.text: Rob's due to make a bloomer in future

indicators.note: to 'make' something of the letters here is to form them into a new word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Rob is about to blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it is a flower; an unopened one is a flower to come. 'make' signals the anagram of ROB'S DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bud is a flower not yet open, so it will bloom later.

clue.text: A German made merrie with it

definitions.text: A German made merrie with it

parts.words: A German made merrie with it
parts.note: the Angles were a Germanic people who settled in Britain and gave their name to a country, and 'merrie' is the old-fashioned epithet attached to that land

explanation.surface: A German had fun with something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angles, a Germanic tribe, gave the country its name (Angle-land), and 'Merrie England' is the stock nostalgic phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The country's name derives from the Angles, a Germanic people, and it is famously called 'Merrie'.

clue.text: They get worn out, following the game

definitions.meaning: hats worn outdoors, the peaked tweed caps of the shooting field
hunters who track deer on foot

explanation.surface: Things exhausted after chasing quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn out' reads as 'exhausted', but it means worn outside, as a hat is; the 'game' is the quarry, deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cap with front and back peaks is named after the hunters who stalk deer, so both hats and hunters share the name.

clue.text: One might use it in travel, off and on

definitions.text: One might use it in travel, off and on

parts.words: One might use it in travel, off and on
parts.note: 'off and on' looks like 'intermittently', but it describes getting off and on a train at a stopping place

explanation.surface: Something a traveller uses now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off and on' seems to mean 'occasionally', but passengers get off and on at the place in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway stop is where travellers board and leave trains.

clue.text: I do more, to make a bit of money

indicators.note: the letters given are worked into a new arrangement, as 'to make' implies forming something

explanation.surface: Someone doing extra work to earn a little cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' signals the anagram of I DO MORE; the answer is an old coin, so 'a bit of money' means one coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A moidore was a Portuguese gold coin also current in England in the 18th century.

clue.text: He is joined by his compatriot in tug-of-war, we are told

definitions.text: He is joined by his compatriot in tug-of-war, we are told

parts.words: He is joined by his compatriot in tug-of-war, we are told
parts.note: the proverb says that when a man of Athens meets another of his nation, then comes the tug of war

explanation.surface: A man teamed with a fellow countryman in a rope-pulling contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'When Greek meets Greek, then comes the tug of war', meaning two equally matched opponents struggle hard; 'we are told' marks it as a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names a native of Hellas meeting his countryman, so the man in question is Hellenic.

clue.text: Tidy numbers of animals, and those who tend them

definitions.meaning: orderly herds; also 'neat' is an old word for cattle

explanation.surface: Orderly groups of livestock together with their keepers.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT is an archaic word for cattle, so the first reading is 'tidy herds' and the second is 'cattle-keepers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat-herds are cowherds, cattle being 'neat' in old English, and taken apart the word is tidy flocks.

clue.text: Girl Santa found wandering on the continent

indicators.note: the letters of the name go astray from their order, as 'wandering' signals

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: A girl finding Father Christmas roaming around a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' makes ANAST from SANTA, placed on ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasia is a female given name, famously a Russian grand duchess.

clue.text: Mythical maiden man adored madly

indicators.note: 'madly' indicates the letters of the two words are scrambled wildly

explanation.surface: A man in a myth adored a maiden passionately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' signals the anagram of MAN ADORED.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda was the princess of Greek legend chained to a rock and rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Ten in play make a picture show

indicators.note: the number goes inside the word for a play, as 'in' says

parts.note: a drama is a play
10 written as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Ten actors in a play putting on a visual spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten is written as figures, 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O, and 'in' places them in DRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene or picture model, once a popular exhibition.

clue.text: Go too far in terms of cricket

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a run is the unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: Overdoing things in the vocabulary of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game; an OVER is six deliveries and a RUN is one point scored, two terms which together make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to exceed a limit, run past a set point.

clue.text: It takes a long time to return to the scene of action

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the phrase for a long time is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: It takes ages to go back to where things happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses AN ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of contest or activity, the setting where events unfold.

clue.text: " The - - and not the deed confounds us "(Macbeth)

definitions.text: " The - - and not the deed confounds us "(Macbeth)

parts.words: " The - - and not the deed confounds us "(Macbeth)
parts.note: Lady Macbeth fears Duncan's murder was tried and failed: the try rather than the act ruins them

explanation.surface: A gap-fill from Lady Macbeth's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth Act 2, Lady Macbeth, hearing a noise, fears 'the attempt and not the deed confounds us': the botched effort, not the murder itself, would undo them.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means a try or effort, set against the completed deed.

clue.text: Authorized to break up bale, in conclusion

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for an ending, as 'in' says

parts.note: an end is a conclusion

indicators.note: breaking up the letters of the word means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Permission given to split a bale, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break up' rearranges BALE into ABLE, and 'in' puts that inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enabled is to be empowered or given authority to act.

clue.text: Tearful state of Hamlet's mother at his father's funeral

definitions.text: Tearful state of Hamlet's mother at his father's funeral

parts.words: Tearful state of Hamlet's mother at his father's funeral
parts.note: Hamlet says his mother followed his father's body 'like Niobe, all tears'

explanation.surface: How Gertrude wept over her dead husband.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet Act 1, Hamlet recalls Gertrude at the funeral 'like Niobe, all tears'; Niobe of Greek myth wept endlessly for her slain children.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective from Niobe, the weeping mother of myth, means inconsolably tearful.

clue.text: Kind of woman any MP, however misogynous, embraces!

indicators.note: the phrase embraces, or holds within it, a run of letters spanning its words

explanation.surface: Even a woman-hating politician hugs a certain sort of woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' marks the run inside aNY MP However; 'misogynous' is only surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph is a beautiful young woman, from the maiden spirits of myth.

clue.text: A bird or two

parts.note: one bird whose name is made of two separate birds' names joined

explanation.surface: One or two birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is one bird, a pipit, and its name splits into TIT and LARK, which are two birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The titlark is an old name for the meadow pipit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Plan to get Diana to put on a little weight

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A scheme to make Diana gain a bit of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like gaining weight, but it simply places A GRAM after DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawing that sets out a design or scheme.

clue.text: Tea-taster perhaps showing skill as a needlewoman

definitions.meaning: one who tries small portions, as a tea-taster does
embroidered cloth worked to display a stitcher's range of stitches

explanation.surface: A tea-taster who is also a skilled seamstress.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries things is a taster, and a stitched panel of letters and motifs shows off embroidery skill.

clue.text: Like the proverbially unsuccessful suitor

parts.note: the proverb says a timid heart never won fair lady

explanation.surface: Describing the wooer who, by the old saying, fails.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Faint heart never won fair lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb's timid lover lacks courage, which is what the adjective means.
